text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Alcatel to ally with Dassault and Aerospatiale to bid for defence electronics group Thomson-CSF.

-- Generale des Eaux to increase stake in media group Havas, move its 20.4 percent holding in pay-TV company Canal Plus into Havas, leaving Havas with 43.5 percent of Canal. Generale des Eaux is also to buy half of Alcatel Alsthom 's 21.2 percent stake in Havas.
-- Government and unions look at ways to alter a 1937 agreement on the organisation of working hours in the banking sector to increase flexibility.
-- Saint Gobain glass group drops bidding for U.S. based Anchor Glass.
-- A shareholder protests the nomination of Thierry Aulagnon as managing director of GAN insurer.
-- Axa-UAP seeks to decrease the ratio of financial groups in its holdings portfolio, sold up to 3.3 billion francs worth of assets last week.
-- Havas capital restructuring is imminent, Generale des Eaux to exchange shares in Canal Plus for shares in Havas.

-- European monetary institute head Alexandre Lamfalussy in an interview says the future European central bank' independence is included in Maastricht treaty, calls for a ministers council on economic policy restricted to the countries taking part in the first monetary union. Says value-added tax and taxes on savings should be consistent throughout the EU, while direct taxes may vary.
-- Investors oversubscribe the first bond issue in euros, partly to avoid the Ecu.
